page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores at a clock frequency of 3.525 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, alongside 2577 GB of bundled local solid-state drive (SSD) storage. The system contains no discrete GPUs. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-threaded computation and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a PassMark memory score ranking in the top 10 percent and recorded 63.59 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Compute metrics demonstrate high throughput in multi-core stress-ng (86377.57) and Geekbench multi-core tests (17837.0). Large block uncached memory bandwidth registers at 124.14 GB/sec for reads and 62.31 GB/sec for writes, falling in the middle tier. Small model LLM inference generates 3042.07 prompt tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly to 2.67 text generation tokens per second on large 70B models due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

The combination of high memory density and 2577 GB of local SSD storage provides favorable resource allocation for data-heavy architectures without requiring auxiliary disk configurations for scratch operations. This hardware setup is appropriate for enterprise database engines, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, large-scale ETL processing, and transactional backends. Tradeoffs include standard single-core execution speed and limited suitability for deep learning workloads that rely on matrix extensions or GPU acceleration.

The instance includes 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage and operates without GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the E64ads_v5 demonstrates top-tier PassMark memory results and strong multi-core execution in stress-ng and Geekbench, complemented by 63.59 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware cryptographic capabilities are enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The instance delivers solid resource density for high-capacity applications, though uncached memory write speeds and complex model inference remain moderate. Its hardware configuration is matched for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database engines, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
